units.function: Embedded-Postgres regression tests for releasing every issue execution/checkout lock owned by a finalized heartbeat Run while retaining retry and unrelated Run ownership.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> heartbeat service cancelRun -> Drizzle/PostgreSQL heartbeat Runs and issue lock columns; no route, runtime driver, worker crash, distributed coordinator or external Agent is exercised.
units.keyDataModels: Company, Agent, heartbeat Run with contextSnapshot.issueId, issue executionRunId/executionAgentNameKey/executionLockedAt and checkoutRunId, plus activity/event/wakeup cleanup fixtures.
units.lifecycle: Seed queued/running Runs and issue lock shapes -> finalize one Run through cancelRun -> bulk-clear all matching locks scoped by company -> preserve pointers already moved to a retry or unrelated Run.
units.testAssessment: The six tests are precise regressions for multi-row orphan cleanup, higher fan-out, missing context identity, cross-company isolation, retry preservation and unrelated Run safety. Sandboxed and approved unsandboxed focused Vitest both skipped 6/6 because embedded PostgreSQL support was unavailable, so none of the asserted database behavior was executed locally.
units.designRationale: A Run can be attached to several issues through legacy wakeup fallback; finalization must therefore resolve ownership by the actual Run foreign-key columns rather than a single context issue, while separate checkout and execution columns protect an already-started retry.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs durable, tenant-safe Work execution leases that recover from worker/Run termination without stranding work or erasing a successor Run, and the evidence chain must distinguish original execution, retry and cleanup authority.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the regression scenarios and bulk, owner-conditional cleanup invariant. Implement a first-class WorkLease/Attempt model with company-scoped relational integrity, compare-and-set transitions, fencing token or generation, expiry/heartbeat, terminal-reason evidence and transactional/outbox finalization; do not reproduce several mutable lock columns on Work as the canonical contract.
units.responsibilityConflict: The test protects operational ownership but represents it as issue columns plus agent-name text, without accountable human, ResponsibilityContract, Approval binding, DataAuthorization, cleanup actor/reason or immutable evidence. A cross-company Run reference is schema-valid even though cleanup is scoped, which is too weak for Company OS responsibility integrity.
evidence: 2026-08-19 sandboxed focused Vitest: collection failed before tests because logger attempted a forbidden default-home write
2026-08-19 sandboxed focused Vitest with task-specific PAPERCLIP_HOME: 6/6 skipped
2026-08-19 approved unsandboxed focused Vitest with task-specific PAPERCLIP_HOME: 6/6 skipped
units.securityFindings: HIGH ownership-integrity gap: schema permits an issue in one company to reference a Run in another and relies on cleanup predicates to avoid cross-tenant mutation. HIGH concurrency gap: no CAS/fencing or cleanup-versus-acquire race is tested. HIGH recovery gap: only cancelRun is exercised, not crash, timeout, kill/reaper or partial-transaction recovery. MEDIUM audit gap: cleanup actor, cause and affected leases are not asserted as durable evidence. MEDIUM test portability gap: all database cases skipped on the audit host.
